title: Derivatives of Exponential & Log Functions
summary: $e^x$ is its own derivative; $\ln x$ differentiates to $1/x$. With the chain rule these give $\frac{d}{dx}e^{g}=e^{g}g'$ and $\frac{d}{dx}\ln g=g'/g$. Logarithmic differentiation tames products, quotients, and variable exponents.

base-a exponential.plain: An exponential with base other than $e$.

logarithmic differentiation.plain: Taking $\ln$ of both sides before differentiating.
logarithmic differentiation.in_class: Turns products/powers into sums — handy for messy functions.

e.in_class: The base that makes the exponential its own derivative.

concept_sections.heading: Derivative of $e^x$ and $\ln x$
concept_sections.explanation: The two headline facts: $\frac{d}{dx}e^x=e^x$ and $\frac{d}{dx}\ln x=\dfrac1x$. Everything else builds on these.

concept_sections.heading: Chain rule versions
concept_sections.explanation: With an inside function: $\frac{d}{dx}e^{g(x)}=e^{g(x)}g'(x)$ and $\frac{d}{dx}\ln g(x)=\dfrac{g'(x)}{g(x)}$.

concept_sections.heading: Other bases
concept_sections.explanation: For base $a$: $\frac{d}{dx}a^x=a^x\ln a$ and $\frac{d}{dx}\log_a x=\dfrac{1}{x\ln a}$. The extra $\ln a$ comes from converting to base $e$.

concept_sections.heading: Logarithmic differentiation
concept_sections.explanation: For products, quotients, and variable exponents (like $x^x$), take $\ln$ of both sides first: it turns products into sums and exponents into factors, which are easy to differentiate.
math_steps: Use log laws to expand, then differentiate implicitly.

concept_sections.heading: Exponential growth models
concept_sections.explanation: Anything growing at a rate proportional to its size satisfies $y'=ky$, whose solution is $y=Ce^{kt}$. The derivative link makes exponentials the natural model.

real_world_examples.title: Radioactive decay
real_world_examples.scenario: A sample loses a fixed fraction each period.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Its amount follows $N=N_0e^{-kt}$; the decay rate is the derivative $-kN$, proportional to the amount left.

real_world_examples.title: Compound interest
real_world_examples.scenario: Money grows continuously in an account.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Balance $A=Pe^{rt}$; the growth rate is $rA$, the derivative — interest on interest.

real_world_examples.title: Sound level in decibels
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Rates of change of a log quantity use $\frac{d}{dx}\ln x=1/x$.
